meta.title: Triangle counts (example)
meta.subtitle: How many triangles can a graph on n vertices have? Blue is realized, rust hatching impossible, dotted grey conjecturally impossible, plain grey still unknown.

nodes.title: Complete graphs K_n
nodes.statement: K_n has C(n,3) triangles, the most a graph on n vertices can have.

nodes.title: The top band is empty
nodes.statement: A graph on n vertices other than K_n has at most C(n,3) - (n-2) triangles.
nodes.note: Proof: a missing edge uv destroys the n - 2 triangles uvw.

nodes.title: One-vertex extension
nodes.statement: Every graph on n vertices is a graph G on n - 1 vertices plus a vertex joined to a set S; the new vertex adds e(G[S]) triangles.

nodes.title: Exact sets for n <= 7
nodes.statement: For n <= 7 the triangle counts that occur are exactly those in frontier.json.
evidence: examples/triangle-counts/make_example.py (one-vertex extension of all graphs on n - 1 vertices)

nodes.title: Only the top band is missing
nodes.statement: Every count from 0 to C(n,3) - (n-2) occurs.
nodes.lesson: Removing edges destroys triangles in discrete amounts, so gaps also appear below the top band: n = 5 misses 6.

nodes.title: The gaps for n = 8
nodes.statement: For n = 8 the counts 37, 42, 43 and 46-49 do not occur.
nodes.test: Extend all 2^21 graphs on 7 vertices by one vertex: about 2.7e8 subset counts, so vectorize or use a cluster.

nodes.title: Gaps come in shifted bands
nodes.statement: Below the top band, the missing counts form bands that follow K_n minus a few edges.
nodes.vivid: n = 6 misses 14, 15 and 17-19. K_6 minus one edge has 16 triangles, minus two edges 12 or 13.

nodes.title: Six unknown counts for n = 8
nodes.next: A larger sample, or the exhaustive test of k.n8.

nodes.title: Kruskal-Katona theorem
nodes.statement: Gives the largest number of triangles for a given number of edges: the upper boundary of the edges-versus-triangles scatter.

frontier_history.why: K_8, K_8 minus an edge, K_7 plus a vertex, and the top band
